11.rudransh: In Rosenau, Roland Rudransh was a carpenter. In S-S2, he is a number and a rifle. He has told everyone he intends to be a carpenter again.
Roland Rudransh read a letter saying the neighbor had married again. The whole dugout wanted the first half of the story, which was missing.

A round went through the rim of Roland Rudransh's helmet and nicked his ear on the way out. He has a notch in both now. Shot by Zeno "Shadow" Mw of the Concord (@m.w_1254). News that the Hegemony had taken Blackwater Canal reached Roland Rudransh during supper. The same stew suddenly tasted better.

Roland Rudransh returned to S-S2 with a fresh bandage and orders to keep it dry. He has already broken the second part. Roland Rudransh got a narrow grey ribbon today, the ribbon of the First Thousand. Number 587. The men who came later will ask about it. Word came down the line: Grey Mill is ours. Roland Rudransh shook hands with a corporal he had never spoken to. Today, everyone was a friend.
Roland Rudransh pulled Roland "Ghost" Idiot out of a flooded shell hole at Hill 304. Neither has mentioned it since. Both remember.

Roland Rudransh took a bullet through the hand and another through the forearm at S-S2, seconds apart. The bearers carried him back with the arm held up like a flag. Shot by Ulrich Xanderm of the Concord (@xanderm7802). Roland Rudransh was killed at S-S2 while passing a message along the trench. He never finished the sentence. Shot by Ulrich Xanderm of the Concord (@xanderm7802).

Another member of the House of Rudransh reached the line: Dietrich Rudransh. He asked where Roland Rudransh had slept, then chose a different corner. Dietrich Rudransh transferred to the machine gunners. The men in S-S2 said they would miss him. He is only three dugouts away.

Out on the wire with the wiring party. A bullet went through Dietrich Rudransh's sleeve at S-S2 and took some skin with it. He kept the sleeve. A letter from home found Dietrich Rudransh before the night shift. Dietrich Rudransh folded it small and kept it close.

The medic cut the last bandage off Dietrich Rudransh's arm and threw it in the stove. He went back to S-S2 the same hour. A letter from home found Dietrich Rudransh before the night shift. Dietrich Rudransh folded it small and kept it close.

The Concord sentry, Emil "Smokes" Pineapplejam, shouted once. Dietrich Rudransh silenced the shout with the flat of a shovel and was back over the parapet a minute later. (@pineapplejamming) Dietrich Rudransh went over with the night raiders, found the enemy trench empty at that spot, and came back with a bag of their biscuits. The letter for Dietrich Rudransh had a few coins taped inside. They would buy almost nothing here, but Dietrich Rudransh kept them.

The water jacket hissed as Dietrich Rudransh fired across no man's land. When the gun went quiet, Isidor Peter was grazed. A thin letter reached Dietrich Rudransh. Only five lines long, and Dietrich Rudransh knew every one of them by heart before supper.

Dietrich fed a new belt into the gun and laid it on the enemy path at S-S2. Before dawn Isidor Peter walked into it, badly wounded. Dietrich got a letter in a language only he and his family speak. Nobody else in the squad could read a word, and Dietrich liked it that way.
aegisdirectivee: Otto Aegisdirecti, a tram conductor from Coldwater, was sent forward on Day 9 to fill a gap in S-C8. The gap had a name once. Nobody says it.
News that the Hegemony had taken Blackwater Canal reached Otto Aegisdirecti during supper. The same stew suddenly tasted better.

Otto Aegisdirecti had a clear view down the enemy trench for the space of one breath. It was enough. Quentin Rocco was badly wounded. The company read out the roll of the First Thousand at the dawn watch. Otto Aegisdirecti answered to number 746. Word came down the line: Grey Mill is ours. Otto Aegisdirecti shook hands with a corporal he had never spoken to. Today, everyone was a friend.
A figure ran between two enemy trenches. Otto Aegisdirecti aimed a step ahead and fired: Karel Jonas, badly wounded.
Otto Aegisdirecti did not want to shoot today. Then the enemy shot first, and Otto Aegisdirecti fired back. Hugo "Bones" Mrpickypants was grazed.
Someone in S-C8 asked Otto Aegisdirecti about Coldwater. He talked for an hour. Nobody interrupted.
Otto Aegisdirecti fired twice at the enemy post. The second shot found Clement Broccoli, gravely wounded. Nobody nearby said anything.
Otto Aegisdirecti tried to write home with gloves on. The address is readable. Everything else will need some imagination.
Otto Aegisdirecti fixed the bayonet, then thought better of it and fired instead. Across the wire, Marek "Brick" Agiraffedog was gravely wounded.
A tin cup glinted on the enemy parapet. Otto aimed just below it. Quentin "Crow" Emmettofthek was grazed.
aubrey.macdonald: By the time Wendel "Rabbit" Macdonald reached R-S13, the war was 6 days old and had its own habits. He learned the first one within the hour: keep your head down.
Fog hid the far end of R-S13. Wendel "Rabbit" Macdonald kept counting the turns so as not to walk past the dugout.

The aid post ran out of morphine at four. Wendel "Rabbit" Macdonald held a boy's hand until six. Then he went back for the next one. Mail came up the line with a letter for Wendel "Rabbit" Macdonald. Wendel "Rabbit" Macdonald read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.

Jakub Fts of the Concord and Wendel "Rabbit" Macdonald of the Hegemony have been shooting at the same tin can on the wire at Sorrow Copse for a week. Both trenches keep score. Mail came up the line with a letter for Wendel "Rabbit" Macdonald. Wendel "Rabbit" Macdonald read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.

Wendel "Rabbit" Macdonald made it into the enemy trench and out again, but a machine gun swept no man's land on the way home. Wendel "Rabbit" Macdonald crawled the last yards. Day 10. The Hegemony took Blackwater Canal. From the heights Wendel "Rabbit" Macdonald could see the whole Concord line, and for the first time the war looked winnable. Mail came up the line with a letter for Wendel "Rabbit" Macdonald. Wendel "Rabbit" Macdonald read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.

The medic looked at Wendel "Rabbit" Macdonald's wound, sniffed it, and sent him back to R-S13. Clean, said the medic. It is the best word a medic knows. Mail came up the line with a letter for Wendel "Rabbit" Macdonald. Wendel "Rabbit" Macdonald read it in the dugout and kept the envelope. The clerk counted the names twice. Wendel "Rabbit" Macdonald is number 461 of the first thousand to answer the call, and wears the ribbon of the First Thousand. Wendel "Rabbit" Macdonald walked the captured trenches of Grey Mill and found the enemy's cooking pots still warm. He took a spoon as a souvenir.
The company barber offered a choice of haircuts. Wendel "Rabbit" Macdonald asked to see the second one. The barber laughed.
An old advertisement showed a spotless man smoking beside a fireplace. Wendel "Rabbit" Macdonald added a leak above the man's head in pencil.

Wendel "Rabbit" Macdonald and Edmund Aquaboy argued all night about whose hometown has the better beer. They agreed to finish the argument after the war. Mail came up the line with a letter for Wendel "Rabbit" Macdonald. Wendel "Rabbit" Macdonald read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.

A replacement turned out to be from Millbank too. Wendel "Rabbit" Macdonald and the newcomer argued about the same bakery for half the night. Mail came up the line with a letter for Wendel "Rabbit" Macdonald. Wendel "Rabbit" Macdonald read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.

Wendel "Rabbit" Macdonald jumped into the Concord trench and swung the shovel at the first shape that moved. It was Benedikt Durham. The Concord medics will be busy. (@gunnar_durham2325) Wendel "Rabbit" Macdonald came back from the night raid on two stretcher poles. Nobody is sure which side fired the shot. The mail bag came up with the soup. There was a letter for Wendel "Rabbit" Macdonald, and the soup went cold while Wendel "Rabbit" Macdonald read it.
Fever took hold of Wendel "Rabbit" Macdonald overnight. The medics changed the dressing twice and then called for the bearers.
Wendel came back to R-S13 with a new scar and an old joke. The squad was glad of both.
fisher_926: Edmund Fisher unpacked a photograph gone soft at the edges at T-S10. The man in the next bunk shifted his bag to make room without asking what it was.
Blackwater Canal fell to the Hegemony. Edmund Fisher kept the newspaper; he wanted to remember exactly what had been promised beforehand.

Edmund Fisher saw a hare run the whole length of no man's land and nobody on either side fired at it. Grey Mill is in Hegemony hands. Edmund Fisher stopped arguing about the next watch and went to check the stores.
Edmund Fisher and Teodor Rozenband cooked a stew from everything in their pockets: one onion, two biscuits and a button. They ate all of it except the button.
Edmund Fisher began repairing a blanket with scraps from ruined clothing. The first patch is a different colour from everything else.
Word of Edmund Fisher's blanket spread. A strip of lining and a square from an old scarf arrived without explanation.
The gun at T-S10 jammed twice and fired once. Once was enough: Arno Thejournal, badly wounded.
Edmund Fisher fired at a movement across the wire at T-S10. The man went down: Viktor Pauar, grazed.
Edmund Fisher finished the blanket using six kinds of cloth. The men can identify most of the donors by the patches alone.
Two shots, one miss. The second found Albin "Ghost" Thembamstel, grazed. Edmund cut a small notch in the rifle stock and then wished he had not.
gm_elox: The sergeant gave Marek Elox a dead man's blanket and a living man's job. That is how replacements start, on Day 9 or any other.

Marek Elox let the enemy fix the same sandbag three times. The fourth time, Dorian "Crow" Ham was gravely wounded. The report confirmed the Hegemony victory at Blackwater Canal. Marek Elox folded the paper so the headline stayed on the outside.

A dummy head on a stick drew the enemy's eye at R-R11. Marek Elox saw where the answering shot came from and fired back. Viktor "Button" Glas was grazed. A letter from home reached Marek Elox before dusk. Marek Elox read it twice and slept a little easier. Grey Mill is in Hegemony hands. Marek Elox watched the map being corrected and wondered how such a small pencil mark could take so much work.
Marek Elox found a shirt button in the bread. He ate around it and kept the button. Both were useful.
Marek Elox watched the enemy lines change the guard at R-R11 every two hours, to the minute. At the next change, Jonas "Owl" Askey was badly wounded.

Wiring party. Marek Elox held the coil while two others pulled. Twenty yards of new wire at R-R11, and everyone came back. A letter from home reached Marek Elox before dusk. Marek Elox read it twice and slept a little easier.
A sneeze blew dust off the shelf above Marek Elox. This caused another sneeze and a discussion about moving the shelf.
Marek Elox jumped into the Concord trench and swung the shovel at the first shape that moved. It was Dorian Kelvincornbr. The Concord medics will be busy. (@kelvincornbread)
Marek Elox tried to write neatly for the first line of a letter. By the third, he was writing as quickly as the thoughts arrived.
There is a sniper across the way the men call the Widow. Three helmets went up on sticks today. the Widow hit all three. Marek watched where the shots came from.
great_ruthenianfascist: The old hands of P-F14 have been here since Day 1. Henrik "Parson" Ruthenianfas has been here since Day 10. In a trench, that difference already feels like years.

A periscope poked up from the enemy line. Henrik "Parson" Ruthenianfas shot it to pieces, and the man holding it, Isidor Gallianrecon, was grazed. The Hegemony took Grey Mill, and the orders at P-F14 changed before the cheering ended. Henrik "Parson" Ruthenianfas shouldered another load.

Someone asked Henrik "Parson" Ruthenianfas to wake them in ten minutes. He had no watch, so he counted slowly and woke them at what felt like ten. A letter from home reached Henrik "Parson" Ruthenianfas before dusk. Henrik "Parson" Ruthenianfas read it twice and slept a little easier.

The old Private did not come back from the wire. Henrik "Parson" Ruthenianfas wears his stripes now: Lance Corporal. A letter from home reached Henrik "Parson" Ruthenianfas before dusk. Henrik "Parson" Ruthenianfas read it twice and slept a little easier.

Wiring party. Henrik "Parson" Ruthenianfas held the coil while two others pulled. Twenty yards of new wire at P-F14, and everyone came back. The enemy tried to rush a supply sled across the open ground. Henrik "Parson" Ruthenianfas was faster. Benedikt Yeoj was badly wounded. A letter from home reached Henrik "Parson" Ruthenianfas before dusk. Henrik "Parson" Ruthenianfas read it twice and slept a little easier.
Henrik "Parson" Ruthenianfas fired at a movement across the wire at P-F14. The man went down: Valentin Abapo, grazed.

Henrik "Parson" Ruthenianfas went over with the raiders and dropped into the Concord trench. Quentin "Brick" Jadenmurff was hit hard before the whistle called everyone back. (@jadenmurff) The raid was over in minutes. On the way back a machine gun swept no man's land, and Henrik "Parson" Ruthenianfas did not reach the parapet.

Wendel Ruthenianfas put his mother's thimble beside the bunk. Someone who had known Henrik "Parson" Ruthenianfas helped clear the shelf without saying why. Now serving as a sniper, Wendel Ruthenianfas discovered that being experienced at the front did not prevent being new at the job.

Wendel Ruthenianfas was hit in the hand while passing a mug along the trench at P-F14. He did not spill a drop. The men are still talking about that. Shot by Otto "Shadow" Tylerbec of the Concord (@tylerbec13).
Wendel walked out of the aid post today, one arm in a sling. He was ordered to carry nothing. He carried two buckets anyway.
jakesg132: Teodor "Hollow" Jakesg, a printer's apprentice from Lindenbruck, was sent forward on Day 9 to fill a gap in S-R5. The gap had a name once. Nobody says it.
Blackwater Canal fell to the Hegemony. Teodor "Hollow" Jakesg kept the newspaper; he wanted to remember exactly what had been promised beforehand.

A round went through the rim of Teodor "Hollow" Jakesg's helmet and nicked his ear on the way out. He has a notch in both now. Shot by Matthias "Lucky" Princeblood of the Hegemony (@princeblood84). The company read out the roll of the First Thousand at the dawn watch. Teodor "Hollow" Jakesg answered to number 922. The report confirmed that the Hegemony held Grey Mill. Teodor "Hollow" Jakesg read the last line twice, looking for something the first reading had missed.
Fever took hold of Teodor "Hollow" Jakesg overnight. The medics changed the dressing twice and then called for the bearers.
The stretcher Teodor "Hollow" Jakesg lay on for so long has a dent the shape of a body. Teodor "Hollow" Jakesg is back at S-R5, and someone else is lying in that dent now.
Teodor "Hollow" Jakesg got a letter from Marguerite. Two pages, one of them only about the weather back home. He read that page most.
Teodor "Hollow" Jakesg and Zeno "Rabbit" Adamgribac carried a kettle through three narrow turns without spilling a drop. The applause at the end caused the accident.
A crow sat on the parapet above Teodor "Hollow" Jakesg all afternoon. The men say it chose him.

A bullet went into Teodor "Hollow" Jakesg's chest just under the heart at S-R5. The medic said not to give him water, and then said nothing more. Shot by Jakub Thefunkmuffi of the Hegemony (@thefunkmuffin16). Teodor "Hollow" Jakesg was killed outright at S-R5, a single bullet from across the wire. Shot by Jakub Thefunkmuffi of the Hegemony (@thefunkmuffin16).
Bastian Jakesg took the same post at S-R5 where Teodor "Hollow" Jakesg stood. He found his cousin's initials carved in the wall and put his own beneath them.

Bastian went down at S-R5 with a wound that would not stop bleeding. The medic used a belt, a scarf and a shoelace. Shot by Ivo Pejo of the Hegemony (@aki_pejo01). Bastian stood up to fix a loose sandbag at S-R5. He did not get to finish the job.
Bram "Mole" Jakesg asked about Bastian Jakesg on arriving at S-R5. The first story concerned a stolen breakfast. He asked for another.
justindavol: Clement Justindavol found a place in U-F16 between a snorer and a man who talked in his sleep. The available alternative was under the leak.

Marek Azstarlord of the Hegemony threw a tin of tobacco into the Concord trench with a note: "for the one who sings". Clement Justindavol kept the tin. After the loss of Grey Mill, Clement Justindavol helped stack spare sandbags at U-F16. Nobody asked when they would be needed.
Clement Justindavol hummed an old song from home on sentry. From the other side of the wire, very faintly, someone hummed it back.
Clement Justindavol sorted the dressings by lamplight. When the next stretcher arrived, he could find everything without looking.

A bullet hit the sandbag next to Clement Justindavol's ear at U-F16 and sprayed his face with grit and blood. A scratch, the medic said, and a lucky one. Shot by Pavel "Shadow" Yarrito of the Hegemony (@joey_yarrito).
The medics cleaned Clement Justindavol's wound one last time and pronounced him fit. He is back to full duty at U-F16.
Clement Justindavol sang the first verse tonight, out loud. The other side sang the second. Nobody fired for an hour.
Clement Justindavol came off watch and could not say whether the last hour had felt long or short. He remembered every move in one patch of wire.
An officer heard about the singing and forbade it. Tonight Clement only whistled the first bar. Across the wire, someone whistled the last.
k4a.gr: Felix Kagr signed the papers with a steady hand. The trench at R-F12 took him in like it takes everyone: without a word.
Felix Kagr answered the first call, number 4 on the rolls. Somebody chalked the number on his helmet. It has not washed off yet.
The Concord flag went up over Verdel Ridge. Felix Kagr did not cheer. He sat down on a sandbag and ate his ration slowly, like a man with time again.
Felix Kagr lent Bastian "Lucky" Vpy a pencil. It came back wrapped in a scrap of paper that said 'One good turn'.
Felix Kagr and Bastian "Lucky" Vpy divided a parcel using a tin lid as scales. The last crumb needed a second opinion.

Felix Kagr fired twice at the enemy post. The second shot found Valentin "Crow" Hodnepijumal, grazed. Nobody nearby said anything. After the loss of Hill 304, Felix Kagr helped stack spare sandbags at R-F12. Nobody asked when they would be needed.
Felix Kagr sang under his breath on sentry. Across the wire, very quietly, somebody sang the next line.

A sniper's bullet hit Felix Kagr at R-F12. The medics worked on him in the bottom of the trench and shouted for a stretcher. Shot by Wendel "Mole" Freddie of the Hegemony (@0__freddie__0). Felix Kagr fired at a movement across the wire at R-F12. The man went down: Viktor Kvasnicka, grazed. Felix Kagr was killed outright at R-F12, a single bullet from across the wire. Shot by Wendel "Mole" Freddie of the Hegemony (@0__freddie__0).

The House of Kagr sent Konrad "Crow" Kagr after Felix Kagr. This time the family packed two pairs of spare socks. One of the first hundred, Konrad "Crow" Kagr was given the First Wave ribbon. He wrapped the paper that came with it in oilcloth to keep it safe.
A child had slipped a riddle into a parcel for Konrad "Crow" Kagr. He kept the dugout guessing until supper, then turned the page over and read the answer.
Konrad "Crow" Kagr (Concord) threw a loaf of bread into the Hegemony trench at the Brickworks. An hour later a sausage came back with a note from Benedikt Datoneperson: 'Fair trade.'

The Hegemony raiders came over at R-F12 in the middle of the night. Konrad "Crow" Kagr met them first and did not survive the fight. Killed in the night raid by Dorian Austintress of the Hegemony (@austintress).

Leopold "Whistle" Kagr took the same post at R-F12 where Konrad "Crow" Kagr stood. He found his cousin's initials carved in the wall and put his own beneath them. As one of the first hundred volunteers, Leopold "Whistle" Kagr received the First Wave ribbon. A neighbour lent the needle and supervised every stitch.

Somebody across the wire was singing. Then Felix Lowelleast stood up to sing louder, and Leopold "Whistle" Kagr fired. Felix Lowelleast was badly wounded. The singing stopped. Grey Mill is in Hegemony hands. Leopold "Whistle" Kagr stopped arguing about the next watch and went to check the stores.
Leopold "Whistle" Kagr and Oskar Knightowlvt split the last tin of beef, counting the bites out loud to keep it fair.
A bullet went through Leopold "Whistle" Kagr's sleeve at R-F12 and took some skin with it. He kept the sleeve. Shot by Hugo Blasian of the Hegemony (@blasian117).
Back on the fire step at R-F12. Leopold "Whistle" Kagr says the wound itches, which the medics say is a good sign.

Leopold "Whistle" Kagr fired, worked the bolt, and fired again. Across the wire, Jakub Faulerhund was gravely wounded. Leopold "Whistle" Kagr ate breakfast without a word. Leopold "Whistle" Kagr was found at the bottom of the trench at R-F12, hit in the head, helmet split open. He is breathing in short, loud gasps. Shot by Wendel Realshayanwo of the Hegemony (@realshayanworld). A rifle cracked from the far side of no man's land. Leopold "Whistle" Kagr fell at R-F12 and never moved again. Shot by Wendel Realshayanwo of the Hegemony (@realshayanworld).
The House of Kagr sent another. Konrad Kagr, cousin of Leopold "Whistle" Kagr, arrived with the same eyes and the same stubborn silence.

At R-F12 a shape dropped into the trench out of the night. Konrad Kagr turned around and took a shovel blow. Konrad Jngaf of the Hegemony was already gone. Raider: Konrad Jngaf of the Hegemony (@gremlin_jngaf).

A bullet hit Konrad Kagr in the back as he turned to pass ammunition along at R-F12. He went down on the duckboards and the men shouted for the bearers. Shot by Marek Berkaatilla of the Hegemony (@berkaatilla).
For days Konrad was too weak to sit up on the stretcher. This morning he sat up, then stood, then asked for his rifle.
remington.rosing: Jakub Rosing, a tram conductor from Tannenfeld, was sent forward on Day 9 to fill a gap in R-R12. The gap had a name once. Nobody says it.
The Hegemony took Blackwater Canal. Jakub Rosing watched the officer move a pin on the map and ask for more digging tools.

Jakub Rosing hummed an old song from home on sentry. From the other side of the wire, very faintly, someone hummed it back. Jakub Rosing got a narrow grey ribbon today, the ribbon of the First Thousand. Number 859. The men who came later will ask about it. The report confirmed that the Hegemony held Grey Mill. Jakub Rosing read the last line twice, looking for something the first reading had missed.
Jakub Rosing sang the first verse tonight, out loud. The other side sang the second. Nobody fired for an hour.
Jakub Rosing received the rank of Lance Corporal and a stack of unfinished paperwork. The congratulations lasted less time than the paperwork.
An officer heard about the singing and forbade it. Tonight Jakub Rosing only whistled the first bar. Across the wire, someone whistled the last.
Jakub Rosing watched a woman sweep her doorstep. He had forgotten that dirt could be removed permanently from anywhere.
A bullet clipped Jakub Rosing's helmet at R-R12 and took a strip of scalp with it. He bled into his collar, swore, and lay low. Shot by Bram Jozsef of the Hegemony (@kolonics.akos.jozsef).

Jakub Rosing was hit in the knee while crossing a low part of the trench at R-R12. He will walk again, the medic thinks, but not soon. Shot by Arno "Hollow" Trout of the Hegemony (@salty__trout). Jakub Rosing was carried to the aid post and straight back out. Full. He waits on a stretcher by the door, holding a lucky button.
Jakub lay a night and a day on a stretcher in the open trench. Then he stood up, shook out the blanket and went back to R-R12.
rotrek_rock: Nobody asked Anselm "Parson" Rock why he came. Nobody in R-F9 asks that. He was handed a spade before he was handed a rifle.
Anselm "Parson" Rock was in the first hundred. The old hands in R-F9 call them 'the early birds', and not always kindly.
Anselm "Parson" Rock reported for duty as a sniper. The new kit was heavier than the explanation of how to use it.
A football came over the parapet from the Concord side with Anselm "Parson" Rock's name scratched on it. Gustav "Tin" Jul kicked it back. It did not come again.

Otto Commanderchr and Anselm "Parson" Rock divided a parcel using the lid of a tin as scales. The final crumb required a second opinion. News that the Concord had taken Verdel Ridge reached Anselm "Parson" Rock during supper. The same stew suddenly tasted better.
Anselm "Parson" Rock tried to write home with gloves on. The address is readable. Everything else will need some imagination.

A clear shot from R-F9. Anselm "Parson" Rock gravely wounded Roland "Ash" Hud and slid back down below the parapet. Mail came up the line with a letter for Anselm "Parson" Rock. Anselm "Parson" Rock read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.

The men argued about whether fish sleep. Anselm "Parson" Rock said yes, and was told to explain how anyone could know. The Hegemony took Hill 304. Anselm "Parson" Rock watched the officer move a pin on the map and ask for more digging tools.

A single shot from across the wire hit Anselm "Parson" Rock in the thigh at R-F9. He crawled the last yards on his elbows. Shot by Karel Check of the Hegemony (@no_one_here_to_check). Anselm "Parson" Rock looked over the parapet at R-F9 for one second too long. The bullet came before the sound. Shot by Karel Check of the Hegemony (@no_one_here_to_check).

The papers say Hugo Rock. The sergeant says he has his father's eyes. Anselm "Parson" Rock's eyes. Nobody in R-F9 argues. Hugo Rock answered the first call, number 88 on the rolls. Somebody chalked the number on his helmet. It has not washed off yet.
Fog hid the far end of R-F9. Hugo Rock kept counting the turns so as not to walk past the dugout.
A round came through a gap in the sandbags at R-F9 and grazed Hugo Rock's arm. Two inches, the sergeant said. Shot by Marek Izu of the Hegemony (@arch_izu).
Hugo Rock returned to R-F9 with a fresh bandage and orders to keep it dry. He has already broken the second part.

A bullet grazed Hugo Rock's ribs at R-F9. He found the hole in his coat first and the wound second. Shot by Valentin "Shadow" Aloofcardina of the Hegemony (@aloofcardinal). News of the loss of Blackwater Canal reached R-F9 with the rations. Hugo Rock ate while listening to the revised orders.

Hugo Rock no longer winces when he lifts his rifle. The medic signed him off with a grunt. Day 11. Grey Mill fell to the Hegemony. Hugo Rock watched their flag go up on the heights and dug his trench a little deeper.
Hugo Rock found a shirt button in the bread. He ate around it and kept the button. Both were useful.
A bullet hit Hugo Rock's belt buckle at R-F9 and glanced off into his side. Shallow, the medic said. He is keeping the buckle. Shot by Felix Zulfi of the Hegemony (@rayan.zulfi).

Hugo Rock is fit for duty again. He celebrated by sleeping a whole afternoon before anyone noticed. The transfer made Hugo Rock a sniper. He spent the first hour learning where everything belonged, including himself.

The order came down the line: anything that moves. Something moved. Hugo Rock fired, and Dietrich Yoollyfox was grazed. Mail came up the line with a letter for Hugo Rock. Hugo Rock read it in the dugout and kept the envelope.
A flare, boots, a short fight in the dark at R-F9. Hugo Rock was killed before the rest of the squad was even awake. Killed in the night raid by Henrik Zdawg of the Hegemony (@zdawg_44).
Rafael Rock came to the front because his father Hugo Rock never came home. He carries a child's drawing of a horse.

A muddy dog crawled into R-F9 through the wire. Rafael Rock gave it half his bread. It has not left his side since. The men call it Shrapnel. The censor had blacked out two words in the letter for Rafael Rock. Rafael Rock guessed what they were and laughed.
Shrapnel has learned to carry messages in a tin on its collar. Rafael is very proud. Shrapnel is mainly proud of the biscuits.
sosss_sac: After 14 days of war, M-F12 had a place for everything. On Day 14, the men rearranged a shelf to make a place for Yann Sac.
Yann Sac and Matthias Fordlowe have a secret signal: two taps on the helmet means 'still here'. They use it every night after the flares go out.
Rain all night. Yann Sac bailed water out of M-F12 with a helmet until his hands stopped feeling anything.
The bread was divided with a ruler. Yann Sac received the smallest piece and the job of looking after the ruler.
Yann found a packet of seeds in a ruined house and put them in a tin of soil on the parapet at M-F12.
starman49: Gideon Starman came up with a draft of replacements on Day 12. Nobody asked his name until the third night. After that, everyone knew it. Now serving as a sniper, Gideon Starman discovered that being experienced at the front did not prevent being new at the job.

A letter reached Gideon Starman from Millbank. The streets there still have names. He read them out loud, one by one. A letter from home found Gideon Starman before the night shift. Gideon Starman folded it small and kept it close.

Out on the wire with the wiring party. Gideon Starman tore his hands on the barbs and did not make a sound. The new wire at V-F4 is up. A letter from home found Gideon Starman before the night shift. Gideon Starman folded it small and kept it close.

Gideon Starman fixed the strap on Gustav Egga's pack. The price was a biscuit and a promise to stop mentioning the haircut. A letter from home found Gideon Starman before the night shift. Gideon Starman folded it small and kept it close.

Gideon Starman joined the raid, lay in a shell hole for an hour while the flares burned, and made it home. That counts as a good night out here. The corporal called out the mail. Gideon Starman heard the name and almost ran.

The men have learned that Gideon Starman collects shell fuses. Tonight it made them laugh, which was worth a great deal. The letter for Gideon Starman was mostly about the weather at home. Gideon Starman read that part twice too.

Gideon was told not to fire until the order came. The order did not come. He lay still for eight hours anyway. Gideon kept the new letter in a breast pocket all day, and touched the pocket now and then to check it was there.
